title: fr.linagora.twalk.inbound.reaction.added.v1
description: A reaction added to a message on an external messaging network, observed as an m.reaction event in a Matrix portal room and normalized by the Sensor as a CloudEvents 1.0 envelope. Produced after successful Megolm decryption. Consumed by Hermes personas subscribed to the inbound.reaction.added.* subject on NATS JetStream. Reaction removals produce no v1 event.

specversion.description: CloudEvents specification version. Fixed to 1.0 for all Twalk v1 events.

id.description: Deterministic identifier computed as sha256(matrix_event_id + ':' + matrix_room_id) of the m.reaction event. Ensures idempotent replay: the same underlying Matrix event always produces the same CloudEvents id.

source.description: URI identifying the Matrix room where the reaction originated. Format: matrix://<homeserver>/<room_id> of the portal room maintained by the bridge.

type.description: CloudEvents type. Reverse-DNS convention with an explicit version suffix. Any breaking change to this schema requires incrementing the suffix (v2, v3, ...) rather than mutating v1.

time.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the Sensor produced the event, not the original network timestamp. The original network timestamp is preserved in data.network_timestamp when available.

subject.description: Matrix user ID of the contact who added the reaction, as materialized by the bridge (e.g. @whatsapp_33612345678:example.com). Used for routing and for consent evaluation.

datacontenttype.description: Fixed to application/json for all Twalk v1 events.

dataschema.description: Optional URI pointing back to this JSON Schema. Recommended for third-party consumers that validate events dynamically.

traceparent.description: Optional W3C Trace Context traceparent header. Enables distributed tracing across Sensor, NATS, Hermes and downstream services without mandating a specific tracing backend.

network.description: Twalk extension. Identifies the external network the reaction originated from, as the user experiences it; transport bridges (e.g. mautrix-gmessages) are never network values. The value matrix is native Matrix traffic: a room with no m.bridge state event and no ghost-prefixed sender, the bring-your-own-account channel (see ADR 0009). Enables server-side filtering on NATS without deserializing the data payload.

consent.description: Twalk extension. Current consent state of the reactor's data-processing agreement, as tracked by the Companion Gateway, the single writer of consent state. Personas MUST refuse to process events where consent is not 'granted', unless they are explicitly authorized to handle consent-management workflows.

reaction.description: The reaction as a Unicode emoji or a network-specific key when the network has no emoji equivalent.

matrix_event_id.description: The Matrix event ID of the message the reaction applies to.

excerpt.description: A short excerpt of the target message, so consumers do not need to look it up to reason about the reaction.

target.description: Structured reference to the message the reaction applies to.

display_name.description: Human-readable display name of the reactor, as known to the recipient.

network_identifier.description: Optional native network identifier (e.g. phone number for WhatsApp, username for Telegram). Only populated when consent state allows it.

avatar_mxc_uri.description: Optional Matrix content URI for the contact's avatar.

contact.description: Structured information about the reactor, resolved by Sensor from the Matrix membership state and bridge metadata.

network_timestamp.description: Optional RFC 3339 timestamp of the reaction as reported by the source network, when the bridge provides it.
